feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. The evidence is iterations 0 to 7. Iteration 1 (324.07) is the stable reference: oval finish 0.70, oval steering_oscillation 0.26, s-bend and slalom max_error about 0.064 m. Iteration 6 reproduced it exactly, so the simulator is deterministic for a fixed design and controller. Every other geometry change lowered the score: 16 mm sensors (iteration 2, oval finish 0.00), wheel_track 0.10 m with kp 4.5 (iteration 3, oval finish 0.10), mass 0.6 kg (iteration 4, 0.30) and mass 0.7 kg (iteration 5, 0.15). Your forward offset to y = 0.06 m is the one untested idea that targets s-bend and slalom max_error, and I have built the controller unchanged so it isolates that offset. Depending on the next race: if the oval finish rate holds at about 0.5 or more and s-bend or slalom max_error falls below 0.06 m, keep y = 0.06 m as the new base. If the oval finish rate falls well below 0.5, return to the y = 0.04 m iteration 1 row, because the controller is tuned to that row and the forward offset costs more than it gains. Do not change body width, since it cannot move the off-track limit within its range.
requested_changes: Keep the forward row at y = 0.06 m only if the oval finish rate is about 0.5 or more and s-bend or slalom max_error falls below 0.06 m, compared with the iteration 1 reference.
If the oval finish rate falls well below 0.5, return to the iteration 1 geometry with the row at y = 0.04 m, and do not pursue further sensor-position changes.
Keep sensor_size at 0.012 m, wheel_track at 0.12 m and mass at 0.8 kg, since iterations 2 to 5 showed each of these lowered the oval finish rate.
